questions.question: For $f\colon A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ with third-order partial derivatives at $a$, what is the third-order derivative tensor $D^3f(a)$?
options: The product $H_f(a)\nabla f(a)$ of the Hessian and the gradient at $a$
The vector $\big(f_{x_1x_1x_1}(a),\dots,f_{x_nx_nx_n}(a)\big)$ of pure third partials
The array $\big(f_{x_ix_jx_k}(a)\big)_{i,j,k=1}^n$ of all third partials at $a$
The number $\sum_i f_{x_ix_ix_i}(a)$, the sum of the pure third partials

questions.question: Let $T=D^3f(a)$ for $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^n)$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$. For vectors $u,v,w\in\mathbb R^n$, suppose $T[u,v,w]=2$ and $T[v,v,w]=3$. What must $T[u+v,v,w]$ equal?

Let $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^2)$ and define $g\colon\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ by $g(x,y,z)=f(x,y)$. How many positions does the raw array $D^3g(a)$ have at $a\in\mathbb R^3$, including positions containing zero?
For $f(x,y)=x^3$ at $a=(0,0)$, both $\nabla f(a)$ and $H_f(a)$ are zero. What does this example show about $D^3f(a)$?
options: A zero Hessian at a point forces the third-order tensor there to vanish.
Third-order information can be nonzero although lower orders vanish.
A zero gradient and Hessian at a point make the function constant near that point.
Only mixed third partials can be nonzero when the gradient and Hessian vanish.

questions.question: If the third partials of $f$ are continuous near $a$, what happens to $D^3f(a)[u,v,w]$ when the three inputs are permuted?
options: It changes sign under each swap of two inputs.
It is unchanged only in the case $u=v=w$.
It is unchanged for all inputs $u,v,w$.
It is unchanged only when $f$ is a polynomial.

questions.question: For $f(x,y)=x^3y^2$, what is the entry $f_{xxy}(1,1)$ of the tensor $D^3f(1,1)$?
For $f(x,y,z)=xyz$, which entries of $D^3f(a)$ are nonzero?
options: Only the pure entries $f_{xxx}$, $f_{yyy}$ and $f_{zzz}$
Six entries, one per ordering of $x,y,z$, each $1$
Only the single entry $f_{xyz}$, which is equal to $1$
All $27$ entries, each of them equal to $1$

questions.question: If $D^3f(a)[u,v,w]=5$, what is $D^3f(a)[2u,v,-w]$?
For $f\in C^3$ in three variables, at most how many distinct values occur among the $27$ entries of $D^3f(a)$?
For $f(x,y)=3x^2-4xy+y^2+7x$, what is $D^3f(a)$ at a point $a$?
options: An array whose only nonzero entry is $f_{xxx}=6$
The Hessian $\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&2\end{pmatrix}$ in each slice
An array that changes with $a$, since $f$ is not constant
The zero array: every third partial of $f$ vanishes

questions.question: For $f\in C^3$, what is the matrix $\big(f_{x_1x_jx_k}(a)\big)_{j,k=1}^n$, the slice of $D^3f(a)$ with first index $1$?
options: The Hessian of the partial derivative $f_{x_1}$ at $a$
The Hessian of $f$ at $a$, multiplied by $f_{x_1}(a)$
The vector of second partials $f_{x_1x_j}(a)$, $j=1,\dots,n$
The first row of $H_f(a)$, repeated in each of $n$ rows

questions.question: Let $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^n)$, $a,h\in\mathbb R^n$, and $g(t)=f(a+th)$. If $g'''(0)=48$, what follows?
options: $h^\top H_f(a)h=48$

questions.question: Let $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^2)$ and $a\in\mathbb R^2$. Suppose $f_{xxy}(a)=6$ and $f_{xxx}(a)=f_{xyy}(a)=f_{yyy}(a)=0$. For a displacement $h=(h_1,h_2)$, what is the cubic term in the Taylor polynomial at $a$?
For $f(x,y)=x^2y$ and any point $a$, what is $D^3f(a)[u,v,w]$ with $u=(1,0)$, $v=(0,1)$ and $w=(1,1)$?
For $f(x,y)=x^4+y^3$, how does the entry $f_{xxx}(a)$ depend on the point $a=(a_1,a_2)$?
options: $24a_1$: it varies with the first coordinate of $a$
$24$ at every point, since $x^4$ has degree $4$
$12a_1^2$: it grows quadratically in $a_1$
$6$, contributed by the term $y^3$

questions.question: For $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^2)$ and $a\in\mathbb R^2$, suppose $f_{xxx}(a)=1$, $f_{xxy}(a)=-2$, $f_{xyy}(a)=0$ and $f_{yyy}(a)=3$. With $e_1=(1,0)$ and $e_2=(0,1)$, what is $D^3f(a)[e_2,e_1,e_1]$?
options: Not determined by the four listed values

questions.question: Let $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^2)$ and $a\in\mathbb R^2$. Suppose $D^3f(a)[h,h,h]=0$ for every $h\in\mathbb R^2$. What must follow about the tensor entries at $a$?
options: Only the pure entries must vanish; mixed entries may remain nonzero.
Only the sum $f_{xxx}(a)+f_{yyy}(a)$ must vanish.
Mixed entries may cancel between their different index orderings.
Every entry of $D^3f(a)$ must vanish.

questions.question: For which $f\in C^3(\mathbb R^n)$ is $D^3f(a)$ the same array at every point $a$?
options: Exactly the polynomials, of any degree
Exactly the functions of class $C^3$ on all of $\mathbb R^n$
Exactly the polynomials of degree at most $3$
Exactly the functions with $D^3f(a)=0$ at every point

questions.question: For $f(x,y)=\mathrm{e}^xy^2$ at $a=(0,1)$, which matrix is the slice $\big(f_{y\,x_j\,x_k}(a)\big)_{j,k=1}^2$ of $D^3f(a)$ with first index $y$, where $x_1=x$, $x_2=y$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: For $f(x,y,z)=x^2z+y^3+xyz^2$ at $a=(1,0,0)$, how many of the $27$ entries of $D^3f(a)$ are nonzero?
